target_translation: For each allowed header name, take the upstream values joined with ", " (strings.Join(h.Values(name), ", "), httpx joins a repeated header the same way), into an http.Header. source_construct: L381: idx.items() replacing each emoji name in the content in turn
target_translation: Keep first-insertion order: a slice of {name, url} plus a map name->index; a repeated tag name overwrites the url at its first position (Python keeps the first position of a reassigned key). Then loop in slice order with strings.ReplaceAll(content, name, img). The result depends on the order when two names overlap in the text, for example ':a:b:' with ':a:' and ':b:' (the first replacement uses the ':' that the second needs). Skip a tag with the warning 'Failed to parse custom emoji' ONLY when tag['name'], tag['icon'] or icon['url'] is missing (the try at :375-379 catches KeyError only). A wrong type (icon not an object, name not a string, tag not an object) raises TypeError/AttributeError in Python, which escapes _clean_html (it re-raises, templates.py:335-336) and fails the render with a 500: return an error there, do not skip.
evidence: templates.py:371-387; idx filled in note.tags order at :373-376; replacement loop :381-385; output is HTML shown in templates; the emoji names have the form ':\w+:' (utils/emoji.py:9), so overlap needs adjacent emojis that share a colon; except clause catches only KeyError (templates.py:377); _clean_html re-raises at templates.py:335-336

target_translation: Port httpx's Response.links: take the 'link' header (repeated Link lines joined with ', '), split with parse_header_links (split on ', *<', url before the first ';', params split on ';' and '=', stopping at a param without exactly one '='), and store each link in an ordered structure keyed by its rel value, or by its url when rel is missing or empty. A repeated key keeps its first position and takes the LAST link's value. Return make_abs(link url, url) for the first key in that order where key != "" and strings.Contains(key, "webmention") (a substring test on the whole rel text, not a token test; 'nowebmention' matches). Use a slice of keys plus a map.
evidence: webmentions.py:31-33, make_abs of resp.links[k].get('url'); httpx/_models.py:753-764 (links builds a dict, key = rel or url, later link overwrites value, keeps position); httpx/_utils.py:175-209 (parse_header_links); the first match wins, so a header with two webmention-like rels returns the first key's link; the result is the endpoint the server posts to
